Commentary.Commentary: So that's all from this game and from  Australia's tour of South Africa. South Africa have bounced back brilliantly after the T20I series loss and have just whitewashed the Aussies. Australia go back home empty-handed in the ODI series. What's next for these two teams? South Africa travel to India to face them in a three-match ODI series, starting on 12th March while Australia will face off against New Zealand which begins on the 13th of March. Join us for all the action! Until then, it is goodbye.

Quinton de Kock, the Protea skipper, says that he is very proud of the boys and they played really well throughout the series. Praises Klaasen for his outstanding performance. On his captaincy, de Kock says that the coaching staff has helped him a lot and it has been a good experience. Adds that they did not start the summer well but this series win showed that they can compete with top sides. On the fresh faces performing, Quinton says that they have shown that they can do well at this level.

Heinrich Klaasen, THE MAN OF THE SERIES, starts by saying that he is happy with his performance. Adds that he has got a couple of injuries but will look to cement his spot for a place in the side. Further says that his hardwork paid off. Klaasen also says he is looking forward to their next series against India.

JJ Smuts, THE MAN OF THE MATCH, starts by saying that it has been a brilliant performance from the team. Adds they did well to restrict Australia to 250 and the bowlers bowled well. Mentions that it is an outstanding achievement for them. Further says they will look to do well against India for their next tour.

The Australian skipper, Aaron Finch says that they have not been at our best. Adds that they have been good in patches and they were put under pressure. Mentions that they need to do their basics right. Further goes onto say that the pressure is always on the top three but the middle order needs to perform. Finch states that that they will look to perform better against New Zealand.

Australia were poor with the bat. Nobody apart from Marnus Labuschagne got going on this wicket an if it was not for Labuschagne, they would not have reached 254. D'Arcy Short too played well but none of the other batters showed application and in the end, it ended up as a below-par score on this wicket. Stay tuned for the presentation...

Earlier in the game, South Africa did really well to restrict Australia to 254. They bowled smartly and every bowler bowled well with Nortje being the best as he picked up 2 wickets. JJ Smuts too bowled well and was well supported by Keshav Maharaj. Overall, they would be happy with their performance.

Australia were disappointing with the ball. They started well, picking up Quinton de Kock and Janneman Malan in quick succession but Kyle Verreynne and JJ Smuts started milking them for runs. Zampa got the wicket of the former but one would feel that Verreynne threw it away. Josh Hazlewood was the pick of the bowlers, giving away just 37 runs and picking up two wickets as well. The other bowlers disappointed and they just failed to hit the right lines and lengths on this wicket.

So, 3-0 it is in favour of South Africa. They were brilliant in this game as they have been throughout the series. One must have thought that 255 would have been a tricky target but the Proteas have made light work of the chase. Even though they lost the openers quite early but then came a brilliant partnership between Verreynne and Smuts which took the home side to a strong position. Once Verreynne fell, it was another show from Klaasen as he got to another fifty in this series. He, along with Smuts played brilliantly and by the time Smuts fell for a valiant 84, the game was done and dusted.

Good length ball around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Good length ball around off, Malan pushes it towards covers.
Landed around off on a length, de Kock looks to work it on the leg side but gets an inside edge on his shoes. Maiden from Richardson.
Play and a miss! Good length ball just outside off, it bounces a bit extra and moves away as de Kock is beaten on his drive.
Good length ball on off, pushed to mid off.
Length delivery on off, de Kock punches it to mid off.
Good shot but straight to the fielder. Good length delivery outside off, de Kock cuts it stylishly but straight to Steven Smith at point.
Fullish and around off, de Kock lunges and defends it out.

FOUR! Pulled away! Short and on middle, Malan swivels and pulls it wide of the man at fine leg. The fielder runs across to his left to cut it off but he fails to reach there. It didn't come from the middle of the bat but it will do for Malan and South Africa.
Landed around off on a length, Malan pushes it towards covers.

FOUR! Wide outside off from Hazlewood and Malan latches onto it in a flash. Malan gets enough room and time to hammer this full and wide ball through cover-point. No chance for any fielder to stop this one.
Landed around off on a length, pushed towards covers.
Good length ball around off, Malan looks to drive on the up again but this time he gets an inside edge on the pads.
Good length ball outside off, Malan looks to punch off the back foot but ends up jabbing it on the pitch on the off side.

FOUR! Poor ball and de Kock puts it away! Sprays this length ball on the pads of de Kock who just helps it on its way to the fine leg fence with a little tickle down the leg side. Jhye shouts in frustration as he knows that it was a poor ball.
Good length ball around off, de Kock comes forward and defends it towards the off side.

Punched nicely! Short and just outside off, Malan hangs on the back foot and slaps it through cover-point. Warner from mid off chases the ball down with a slide before the ropes. Three taken before the throw can come to the keeper.
Quick single! Full and just outside off, de Kock drives it towards mid off and takes a quick single.
Full and on the pads, flicked towards the leg side.
Short and wide outside off, de Kock slaps it straight to the point fielder.
Length ball around off, Malan pushes it towards covers.
Fuller and around off, de Kock flicks it through mid-wicket. Zampa from mid on chases the ball down with a sliding effort and saves a run for the side.
Landed on a length and on middle, de Kock does well to keep it out off his back foot as he ends up getting an inside edge onto the pads.
Fuller but outside off again, de Kock is not lured into going for the drive as he covers his stumps and lets it go to the keeper.
Fuller and around off, this one is flicked towards mid-wicket.
Good length ball just outside off to begin from Hazlewood. De Kock makes a leave.
Josh Hazlewood to bowl from the other end with the second new ball.
Good length ball around off and middle, de Kock looks to flick but the ball takes a thick outside edge and goes towards third man for a single. 6 from the first over.
Length ball outside off, de Kock lets it go to the keeper.
Good length ball outside off, de Kock thinks of leaving it but is late in doing so. The ball catches the outer part of the bat and goes to short third man.
FOUR! De Kock is off the mark in style! Richardson overpitches it just a hint and bowls it outside off, de Kock comes forward and drives it through mid off for a boundary.
Landed around middle and leg on a length, de Kock blocks it onto the pitch on the leg side.

Malan and South Africa are underway! Richardson starts with a full ball just outside off, Malan looks to drive but the ball moves a hint away and takes the outside edge. It goes towards third man for a run.

We are back for the chase. The Australian players are out in the middle. Quinton de Kock and Janneman Malan will open the innings for South Africa. Jhye Richardson will start the proceedings for Australia with the first new ball.
